title: VPC CD policy and Helm values freeze
body:
Context:
This is a working runbook for how we promote artifacts into VPC/on‑prem clusters using GitOps (Argo) and Helm with a short values freeze window. Goal: make upgrades predictable for enterprise customers while preserving a clear emergency rollback path and minimal operator touch. This doc focuses on the CD policy, the Helm values freeze process, Terraform hooks for promotion, and the required signing/provenance checks for air‑gapped or tightly controlled VPC installs.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Enforce a brief Helm values freeze (2 hours default) for any production promotion to customer VPCs unless marked emergency.
- Require signed OCI manifests + cosign attestations (or equivalent) before Argo will accept changes into the customer app repo.
- Use Terraform promotion hooks (pre-promo and post-promo) to run smoke checks and reconcile operator permissions.
- Keep an automated rollback label on promoted releases for 72 hours to enable fast rollback by SRE/customer-ops.

When to apply this runbook:
- Any release that touches control-plane components (operator, admission webhook, cert-manager integration) or model-serving images.
- Upgrades that change HelmChart API versions, CRD changes, or alter persistent storage claims.

Definitions:
- Promote: the process of moving an artifact from staging registry/tag to the customer-facing registry/tag and updating Argo app repo to point at the new chart/image.
- Values freeze: brief period where chart values are not changed while the promotion completes and smokechecks run.
- Provenance: signed metadata proving artifacts were built by the CI pipeline and passed tests.

Pre-promotion checklist (owner: release engineer):
- Confirm PR in helm-charts repo has two approvals and CI is green (link referenced in linked_artifacts).
- Ensure image manifests are cosign-signed and an attestation artifact exists. If customer is air‑gapped, ensure the signed bundle has been exported per airgap bundle spec.
- Verify Terraform promotion hook scripts exist in infra-release repo and are set to run against the target workspace.
- Open promotion ticket in JIRA with target cluster(s), freeze window, rollback owner, and approvers.
- Notify customer-ops and account team at least 24 hours before planned promotion (unless emergency).

Helm values freeze policy (default):
- Freeze window defaults to 2 hours before and 1 hour after promotion entry into Argo (total 3 hours).
- During freeze: only emergency exceptions allowed via an explicit rollback/patch RFC in the promotion ticket.
- Owner can extend freeze to up to 6 hours for high-risk changes with exec approval.
- Enforcement: we add a CI check that blocks merges to the customer-values repo during the freeze window. The check reads a promotion lock file in the repo.

Terraform promotion hooks (pattern):
- pre_promo.sh (run via GitHub Actions or release controller):
  - Validate terraform plan for the customer workspace (no drift on operator roles).
  - Ensure KMS key rotation times are respected; do not promote during KMS maintenance windows.
  - Run a dry-run smokecheck (kubeconfig to staging copy) to verify helm template renders and CRDs apply.
- post_promo.sh:
  - Confirm Argo has applied the new commit and apps are Healthy for at least 2 consecutive reconciles.
  - Run integration smoke tests listed in the promotion ticket (API health, sample infer request, KV cache warm).
  - Emit promotion result to ticket and call webhooks to billing/observability.

Image signing & provenance enforcement:
- Required for all customer promotions. Acceptable schemes: cosign with TUF-like attestations, or OCI layout bundles with detached signatures.
- CI must publish both the image:tag and a signed SBOM/attestation into the artifact registry.
- Argo admission controller (we run a lightweight policy engine) will reject updates where signatures/attestations are missing or invalid. The admission webhook is configured in the customer-values repo via a config map pointing at allowed keys.
- For air‑gapped installs: operator must be provided with offline attestation bundle; we store a signed digest in the tf workspace secret for verification.

Promotion flow (step-by-step):
1) Prepare release PR in helm-charts + copy change into customer-values repo (branch: release/PRNUM-promote).
2) Run pre_promo.sh; if any step fails, abort and log failure into JIRA.
3) Tag images in the customer registry (or create image mirror in airgap proxy); push and cosign.
4) Update values.yaml reference to new image digest, commit, and push to customer-values branch.
5) Create Argo App commit by merging customer-values branch into the repo monitored by Argo (merge gated by the freeze lock).
6) Argo reconciles; post_promo.sh runs after two healthy reconciles.
7) If health checks fail, trigger rollback flow described below.

Rollback and emergency patches:
- Rollback label: every promotion commit is labeled with prometheus-style metadata and a rollback token stored in the promotion ticket. Token valid for 72 hours.
- Automated rollback path: release controller reverts app commit to previous commit and executes post_rollback.sh which verifies app health and rotates any ephemeral secrets used during promotion.
- Emergency patch: bypass freeze only if the ticket includes incident justification and two approvers (SRE lead + product security).

Compatibility matrix notes (Terraform module considerations):
- We must maintain tf module inputs backward compatibility for at least two previous minor versions. Major changes require a migration plan and customer opt-in.
- Modules that touch network policy, cluster endpoints, or service CIDRs are HIGH RISK and should not be promoted in the same window as core operator upgrades.
- Provide a tfplan diff artifact in the promotion ticket for reviewers.

Operator upgrade checklist (Helm/CRD focused):
- If CRDs change, ship CRD-only pre-release chart first (apply CRDs via a one-time job). Wait 24 hours for CRD conversion hooks to settle before rolling operator pods.
- Never combine CRD schema migrations + heavy traffic model version upgrades in the same promotion.
- Use helm hooks to drain a small percentage (default 10%) of nodes/pods for safe cache warming.

Monitoring & observability during promotion:
- Create a short-lived dashboard for the promotion window that shows: latency P95 for model endpoints, error rate, host GPU utilization, and pod restarts.
- Configure alerting for any error-rate > 5% or pod restarts > 3 in 10 minutes. Alerts route to oncall and customer-ops.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we integrate the Argo admission signature check with customers who run their own KMS? (proposal: support external key lists uploaded to the customer-values repo as a allowed keyset).
- Confirm exact SBOM format for airgap bundles (CycloneDX vs SPDX). Action: Maya to pilot CycloneDX bundle in next promotion.
- Decide default freeze window per customer tier (enterprise customers probably need longer). Action: product to define tiers.

Appendix: example promotion ticket template (short)
- Title: promote operator vX.Y.Z to customer acme-corp: cluster-prod-1
- Stage: pre-promo checks completed / freeze window: 2025-02-10T09:00–12:00 UTC
- Artifacts: image digests, cosign signature references, SBOM link
- Terraform plan link: include plan artifact URL
- Approvers: release-engineering lead, customer-ops, security reviewer
- Rollback token: autogenerated string (set by release controller)

Notes to self (rough):
- Implement a small GitHub Action to place/remove freeze lock file and post a comment to JIRA.
- Add a promotion-mode flag to the Helm operator that disables auto-upgrade of built-in CRs during the 3 hour freeze.

References (internal):
- Confluence: promotion playbook (CONFLUENCE-PRIVDEPLOY-42)
- GitHub: helm-charts PRs and infra release hooks (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: promotion queue JIRA-7281

End of draft.
